stances.reasoning: Cast the sole dissenting vote (1-8) against the February 2025 citywide upzoning ordinance; called the competing three-story proposal 'the lesser of two evils' but voted against that too. Reflects a position of protecting existing neighborhood character strictly and requiring community process before any rezoning.

Argued that form-based coding must precede any zoning change (warning of a 5-year implementation lag) and expressed concern about irreversible consequences of rapid upzoning. Her position is to allow growth only where design controls and infrastructure are already in place.

Advocates the Cambridge Land Trust model, inclusionary requirements, and targeting low-to-middle-income housing development — but rejected the citywide upzoning mechanism as the tool to achieve it. Her approach reflects targeted subsidies and easier permitting for affordable projects rather than either public housing construction or a pure market approach.

Voted 5-4 in April 2025 to restore two-way car traffic on Garden Street against the Transportation Department's expert safety recommendation. Cambridge Bicycle Safety did not designate her a bike champion. Her vote prioritizes road capacity and car traffic flow over bike infrastructure.

Directly supported wraparound services at the Transition Wellness Center shelter but ultimately accepted the fiscal-driven shelter closure. No criminalization posture found. Reflects investment in outreach and shelter services while enforcing reasonable fiscal constraints — neither housing-first absolutism nor enforcement-first.
